summary.en: The account restates thresholds, rest, recurrence, merges and openness in discrete steps and whole amounts, by its own verdict restated, level or states less; where it agrees it is mostly with laws its records credit to the field. It states exact thresholds for the fold's form, a periphery fold and transcritical end, per-graph threshold laws, a critical-mass band in a constant, bounds on carried differences and cycle witnesses. It has no law of hysteresis or a path through a band, Hopf crossing, critical rate of a regime, escape time beyond geometric bounds, an absorbing-state transition, Turing's instability, self-organized criticality, percolation or dissipative structure; bounded chaos stands only in a history page. Compositions for hysteresis and rate stay here as proposals, not results. It diverges on the attractor, on a phase transition's word, on direction, and with a cycle under mutual support against Thomas's rule for flows. I looked for contrary reading and found none.

name.en: The saddle-node (fold) and the harvested equilibrium

source.work: Guckenheimer and Holmes, Nonlinear Oscillations, Dynamical Systems and Bifurcations of Vector Fields (1983); Clark, Mathematical Bioeconomics (1976); May, Nature 269 (1977)

sense.en: A stable and an unstable equilibrium meet and vanish as a parameter passes a critical value. Generically the local form is x' = r + x²: the equilibria part as the square root of the distance to the fold, and just past it a run lingers in a bottleneck whose passage time grows as the inverse square root. Under a harvest with depensation the unstable branch is a threshold level.

reading.en: The regime's `Short` and `Meets` are the sign of giving less the draw. `H + y` is the exact point between the fates and reads as the unstable branch; it is a fixed point of the step only where giving at y equals the draw, since whole-number giving can jump past it. A draw beyond all giving ends the condition from every level, which reads as past the fold. The periphery takes the fold's local form separately, as a chosen model. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (the regime; any giving law, whole numbers): where giving falls short of the draw below y, gives nothing from nothing, meets it at every z from y with z + H at most a top hi the step keeps, and 0 < H + y, a level up to hi ends exactly where it starts below H + y. The time to break lies in a band.
The margin of a regime is harvesting under depensation and the fold (Clark 1976; May 1977), in whole numbers.
Record, periphery, discrete steps: at a fold, x + h (m − x²) with rest √m, the multiplier is 1 − 2h√m; it rises to one as the margin m goes to zero, and m = ((1 − a) / (2h))².

account_adds.en: Exactness for any giving law in whole numbers; rises of joint draws superadditive up to one; and `Notch`, a witness that without giving rising with what is left no level separates the fates. S-12 asks whether this adds anything to the continuous analysis; it is unanswered.

source_adds.en: Continuous theory states that the local form is generic, with its unfolding, and the bottleneck's inverse-square-root time. Here a level falls below b within any n with x < b + (H − Y)n: a bound inverse in the draw less the most given, not a passage law. The form is a model taken, not joined to the whole-number point. The record says the fold over the reals and the other order of a step are not stated, and yeast past its fold broke days before the constant-regime curve said.

name.en: The transcritical bifurcation and the threshold at rate one

source.work: Kermack and McKendrick (1927); Harris, The Theory of Branching Processes (1963); Diekmann, Heesterbeek and Metz, J. Math. Biol. 28 (1990)

sense.en: Two equilibria cross and exchange stability at a threshold. The zero state loses stability where a growth factor passes one, for webs where the spectral radius of a next-generation matrix does (R0). Above it a positive branch appears; a branching process at or below one dies out almost surely, except in the trivial case of exactly one offspring.

reading.en: The periphery's damped and web laws have the threshold's linear form: a + r against one, and a rate against one. The logistic drawn model has one transcritical end, its rest going to nothing as the draw reaches the renewal rate. The core's whole-number loop has no gradual side: it closes at once, keeps, or exceeds every bound. The account does not join these, and the web law has no positive branch: past the threshold it runs away. That they are one threshold is my reading. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (periphery): with damping factor a, coupling at every step, D > 0 and a + r ≥ 0, a held loop stays bounded exactly where a + r ≤ 1. A web coupled at every step vanishes below rate one and runs away above it. At rate one, the rate does not decide whether it stays bounded.
Theorem (any type): with whole-number factors a loop closes at once, keeps, or exceeds every bound, never closing gradually (`LoopReturn.nothing_between`).

Theorem (periphery, discrete steps, one variable linearized about a rest): at a transcritical end under a proportional draw, a rises to one as the margin shrinks. Record: under logistic renewal with a proportional draw, rest K (1 − q / r), the multiplier is 1 − h (r − q), so the stock slows in proportion to its own level.

account_adds.en: At rate one the law undecides: the identity is bounded and a shear carries 1 + n, both rate one. Stated in any normed ring. In whole-number factors nothing lies between closing at once and keeping, so decay below one belongs to the periphery's damping.

name.en: Hopf bifurcation and oscillation from delay

source.work: Hopf (1942); Marsden and McCracken, The Hopf Bifurcation and Its Applications (1976); Hutchinson, Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. 50 (1948); May, Nature 261 (1976); Thomas (1981) on circuits

sense.en: As a parameter passes a value a complex pair of eigenvalues crosses into instability and a small limit cycle is born, its amplitude growing as the root of the distance, its period set by the eigenvalue (on maps, the flip and Neimark–Sacker cases). Delay in a negative loop alone can do it. Thomas's rules say which circuits oscillation and multistability need.

reading.en: No eigenvalue crossing here, so Hopf's form fails. What the account states is overshoot by late reading, with exact onset for one relay: past a stated bound it leaves the band at both ends without end. That is oscillation from lateness in an opposing rule, at full swing from its onset, not the smooth birth of a small cycle. `Alternation`, a period-two witness nearer the flip of overcompensating maps, gives two from nothing, so it lies outside the regime's premise that nothing gives nothing. That this lateness is the source's delay is my reading; no record credits Hopf or Hutchinson. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World; balance at the condition): the bound is exactly no overshoot (`Flow.withinGap_iff_between`); within it, opposing, the level settles at m; beyond it an opposing exchange crosses and can oscillate for ever. With a ≤ b, 0 < a, 0 < M and the floor (ℓ + 1)M ≤ b + 1, every balanced run of a relay reading ℓ steps late, from every start below a held for its first ℓ + 1 steps, settles in the band exactly where a + (ℓ + 1)M ≤ b + 1. Record: a relay entering its band does not settle there in general: past b + 2 ≤ a + (ℓ + 1)M the start held at a − 1 leaves both ends without end (`held_oscillates`).

Overcompensating giving can cycle for ever (`Alternation`), a witness: giving two from nothing and nothing from more keeps a band up to two under a draw of one, yet the run from one moves between one and two at every step.

Beyond a band support can sustain a cycle (`Relay.cycles`, a witness): each gives two only where enough is left of the other; under draws of one each alone ends from every level, while from two and three the run moves between two and three and three and two for ever.

Correspondence field: the overshooting thermostat's cycle is the limit cycle of an over-compensating on-off controller. A toy rule; the record lists a heater that reads late among what it does not show.

name.en: Deterministic chaos, and what whole numbers exclude

source.work: Lorenz, J. Atmos. Sci. 20 (1963); Li and Yorke, Amer. Math. Monthly 82 (1975); May, Nature 261 (1976); Costantino and others, Science 275 (1997); Henson and others, Science 293 (2001)

sense.en: Bounded deterministic motion can be aperiodic and sensitive to its start, in very simple maps and flows, so determinism does not give long prediction from finite precision. Costantino and others report a chaotic regime in flour beetle cultures; Henson and others report lattice effects, the whole-number states pulling a chaotic model's dynamics toward cycles.

reading.en: Chaos stands only in a history page. Proposed here as a structural reading, which no live text draws: the nearest live form is how far a difference can grow. Through a loop the carried amount reaches D(1 + M)^t, attained; with none upstream it stays polynomial. That is stretching without folding, a worst case over laws: no one law's sensitive dependence, no bounded aperiodic motion. Likeness to a Lyapunov bound is my reading. A finite web's run within a bound repeats; the root's laws on any type do not exclude a shift. T2's beetle archive comes from the group reporting chaos; T2 says nothing of it. [AI reading]

Theorem (World): under the standard bounds the carried amount is at most D(1 + M)^t, attained by a self-loop; with stationary strengths the gap is bounded by a polynomial in the steps, uniformly over laws, exactly where no loop lies upstream. name.en: Undecidable long-run behaviour and computational irreducibility

source.work: Moore, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64 (1990); Wolfram, Phys. Rev. Lett. 54 (1985)

sense.en: A low-dimensional system embedding universal computation has long-run questions, such as whether a run enters a set, that no procedure decides for every start. So exact knowledge of state and law need not give the long run, apart from any sensitivity to the start. Wolfram argues further that for some systems no shortcut beats running them; how general that is stays disputed.

reading.en: Proposed here: the account has this question's logical form. Within a list a run makes fewer than N changes, yet whether it changes again is decided only as a premise, and every run settling is exactly LPO, which computable models refute by the halting problem. Within a bound the question is a finite check. But LPO measures constructive strength, not computability, and no law embeds a universal machine, so no undecidable dynamics is stated. The link is mine; no record draws it. [AI reading]

says.en: Calibration (any process): a run within a list of N configurations with no change within a loop makes fewer than N changes and settles exactly where it is decided at every step whether it changes again. Exactly LPO: in every world of decidable configurations that a list holds, every run from a configuration with no reachable change that can be undone settles. The number of changes is bounded, but the step of the last change is not.
The theorem says rest cannot be refuted, not when it comes: naming the step after which nothing arises gives LPO (`World.lpo_of_finite_ends`).
A run within B repeats within (B + 1)^n steps, so ending is a finite check with no band, on a finite web read condition by condition.

Theorem (any type): where a map moves every value, no member of a family of readings indexed by what it reads says the diagonal gap. Record: 'Gödel's incompleteness and the halting problem lie outside its laws: arithmetic coding and provability are not stated.'

account_adds.en: What a long-run claim costs in logic, stated law by law, with the finite-check side exact.

name.en: Hysteresis: distinct collapse and recovery thresholds

source.work: Noy-Meir, J. Ecol. 63 (1975); Ludwig, Jones and Holling, J. Anim. Ecol. 47 (1978); Scheffer and others, Nature 413 (2001)

sense.en: Between two folds a system has two stable states, so a parameter that drives a collapse at one value must be taken back past a different value before recovery. Which state holds depends on the path of the parameter. A loop of forward and backward thresholds is the phenomenon; the width of the band sets how costly restoration is.

reading.en: Proposal, not a result: no live law states this, and it stands as a candidate for the atlas to prove. In the stag hunt (shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected; c is a constant there, so moving it is the proposal) with lo ≤ hi, raising c past hi loses the shapers' lock; brought back within (lo, hi), the others' lock holds until c ≤ lo, given some shapers left: distinct thresholds, width hi − lo, whose edges are a critical mass meeting an end, not folds. In thresholds-of-waiting's triad tolerance zero collapses, one keeps either state, two restores. Both compositions are this crosswalk's. The records' word 'hysteresis' names memory in giving and a final ending. [AI reading]

account_adds.en: Not the loop: the exact premises of the one-sided case, each with a witness: below a need with no raising exchange a level does not return (`Flow.never_returns_below`); where nothing gives nothing, an ended level stays nothing whatever the draw later does, so that branch has no recovery threshold (this crosswalk's composition). An end absorbs while requirements do not loosen; a dissolved requirement is transformation, not recovery. Restoration by joint net giving is a law of every balanced flow.

source_adds.en: The phenomenon as a law: two thresholds of one path, a parameter run forward and back, the band's width as restoration's cost. No live text states these. On a renewing regime under a draw no band is stated; the plan's CY(b) would, and its hysteresis test holds until then, on a 'no law' the proposal above does not lift. name.en: Tipping by rate

source.work: Wieczorek and others, Proc. R. Soc. A 467 (2011); Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 370 (2012); Scheffer and others, Ecosystems 11 (2008)

sense.en: A system can leave a state that stays stable for every frozen value of the parameter, because the parameter moves faster than a critical rate and the system cannot track it. No bifurcation need occur. Ramped past a fold slowly, by contrast, a system tips later than the static threshold, by a delay with its own scaling.

reading.en: Proposal, not a result. name.en: Tipping by noise and escape times

source.work: Kramers, Physica 7 (1940); Freidlin and Wentzell, Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems (1984); Horsthemke and Lefever, Noise-Induced Transitions (1984)

sense.en: In a regulated state noise carries a run over a barrier. The mean time to escape grows exponentially in the barrier height over the noise strength, and a quasi-potential says which route and which state hold in the small-noise limit. Noise can also create states that the deterministic system lacks.

reading.en: Noise leaves locks, and in one case a regulated pair: the window absorbs errors it spans, and a burst leaves for good, with survival falling geometrically. A barrier in burst length is a discrete relative of escape, by my reading; the bound counts only aligned bursts, so it is loose. The unregulated walk's Chebyshev-type bound differs in kind. The capture chain's product of weights is a nearer relative of a quasi-potential, also my reading; the records credit Kandori and Young. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (two values, natural weights, independent steps): the courses of n steps reaching the need take at most n·p·q/m² of the weight, Kolmogorov's maximal inequality in counting form. Reading: the unregulated case; void from n = m·m/(p·q). It is not the regime's point of no return.

Theorem (errors only withhold, natural weights; near-definitional once errors are one-way and a law keeps mutual withholding): where both formations err at two consecutive steps, a pair of such laws withholds at every step from then on. Of the courses of 4k values, whose weight is ((p + q)^4)^k, those still giving at step 2k weigh at most ((p + q)^4 − p^4)^k. That the share falls to nothing is by hand.

Drawn one member at a time, the stag hunt leaves either lock by drift, at a weight of at most t times the product of down over up across the counts s + 1 to s + n. A time to leave a lock beyond the geometric bound is not stated.

Reading [AI, over the proved cases]: a lock read from a population drawn anew is kept for good only without noise, or where the rule leaves the disfavoured kind nothing; counts that accumulate are an urn with increasing returns (cited, not stated).

account_adds.en: Bounds in exact counts, and a record law: given the weighting, a record bears on the exit only through the margin it shows and the steps it leaves. Computed, not proved: at an error chance of 1/20, total withholding comes after about 30 steps under answering and about 3×10⁴ under the window of two.

source_adds.en: Continuous theory states the exponential law and its prefactor, the quasi-potential, the most likely route, and noise creating states. The record says exponential exit bounds within a horizon are not stated, nor unbalanced walks. A regime with renewal has no law of noise-driven exit; the pair's law holds for one-way errors alone. 08 lists the risk-dominant state as noise vanishes as not stated; 02's Open lists the time to leave a lock.

name.en: Absorbing-state transitions

source.work: Harris, Ann. Probab. 2 (1974); Janssen (1981); Grassberger (1982); Hinrichsen, Adv. Phys. 49 (2000)

sense.en: A nonequilibrium system with a state it cannot leave can show a sharp transition between an active and an absorbing phase as a parameter passes a critical value, with exponents shared across a universality class (directed percolation is conjectured generic). In a finite system absorption is certain eventually; sharpness belongs to the limit of infinite size.

reading.en: The account states absorption at several grains, and the premises for it, in laws that are per course and finite. It has no parameter sweep of a density and no large-size limit, so what it has is the state's closure, not the transition. A finite chain reaching its absorbing state is credited by one record, 'by hand'. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type): a configuration is drawn into some absorbing region exactly where it does not return. Near-definitional, not a classical attractor.

Theorem (World): the end absorbs: under balance, only active formations giving and activity needing support, once nothing is supported, while requirements do not loosen, nothing is supported or active again. Each premise is needed; dissolving a requirement is transformation, not recovery.
In sampled generations the ends absorb; the histories still mixed after k cohorts weigh at most r^k of (N^N)^k, finite bounds.

Correspondence field: 'a chain with a reachable absorbing state reaching it with probability one'. Law: a pair of laws keeping mutual withholding, after a burst of one-way errors, withholds from then on; that the share falls to nothing is by hand, a ratio of the weights.

account_adds.en: Witnesses for each premise of absorption (a requirement dissolving, a give from beyond, an idle giver, a giver unsupported, a rise from nothing), which names what would leave the state.

source_adds.en: The transition itself: the critical parameter, order parameter, exponents, universality, and a metastable lifetime growing with size. All of these need densities and an infinite-size limit that the account does not represent. Its Not-shown says no universal phase threshold between regions.

name.en: Critical slowing down

source.work: Wissel, Oecologia 65 (1984); Scheffer and others, Nature 461 (2009); Dakos and others (2008, 2012)

sense.en: Near a bifurcation the rate of return to a state falls to zero, so its variance and autocorrelation rise beforehand. These can serve as generic indicators of an approaching transition, read from rolling windows of a single series.

reading.en: The periphery proves the stationary formulas of the linear step at a fixed multiplier, stationarity supplied, and that the multiplier goes to one in two chosen models, a fold's form and a logistic with a proportional draw. So the law has the field's form in a linear one-variable case. It is credited, and the record says the theory adds only the reading (see the next entry). [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (periphery; discrete steps, one variable linearized about a rest, deviation and noise independent with finite second moments): variance Var E/(1 − a²) where a² < 1, lag-1 autocorrelation a; at a fold and a transcritical end under a proportional draw, a rises to one. Nonlinear runs, finite windows and several variables are not treated.

account_adds.en: The reading: no one function of the multiplier returns the margin to a need for every need (`SlowingDown.need_not_read`), by construction. In the logistic drawn model with h, r and K nonzero a measured need's margin is read off the multiplier, with the model known (`SlowingDown.need_margin_read`), likewise by construction.

source_adds.en: The signal in use: the record excludes rolling-window convergence, red noise, several variables, flickering, noise-induced transitions, shifts with no bifurcation and the linearization's error near the fold, all of which the field treats. Continuous-time diffusion forms are also unstated.

name.en: How far early warnings reach

source.work: Scheffer and others, Nature 461 (2009), on generic signals; Boerlijst, Oudman and de Roos (2013); Dekker, von der Heydt and Dijkstra (2018); Hastings and Wysham, Ecol. Lett. 13 (2010)

sense.en: The field's general reading is that rising variance and autocorrelation warn of a coming critical transition across many systems. Later work in the field qualifies this: a warning shows only in what carries the critical mode, a leading system's indicators may ignore whether a follower tips, and shifts can come with no warning at all.

reading.en: T6 confines the signal: the statistic reads the observed condition's own rate of return, and a dependent's need is no bifurcation of that renewal. The confinement is the later literature's too: the audit says the uncoupled side holds by construction in matched form and is the eigenvector literature's, and the chapter says that literature refuted T6's first wording. So this is scope with no third part. Its empirical content, negligible feedback, no test has measured. [AI reading]

says.en: Thesis T6: a break is seen coming only through what couples into what breaks; invisible half proved on the World model, seen half periphery, one law across domains and 'only where' outside these models conjectured. Forbids: given the stock's own course, its statistics separating runs where a dependent's need is crossed from runs where not, the dependent taking no measurable share. Three frozen seabird tests did not reject it: low power, estimates in the refuting direction (about 0.3); power about 0.9, near zero, reusing rows; power about 0.5, feedback argued, not measured. None establishes conditional independence.

Theorem (World): where that stock is the only requirement that may fail up to a horizon, some raise of it is alike through the couplings and supports the formation to the horizon: how far off the break is does not couple in.
Audit: 'the uncoupled side holds by construction in matched form and is the eigenvector literature's'. Dekker and others (2018) named as the closest prior form of the uncoupled side.

Theorem (World: balance; nothing given): where each step's draw exceeds everything drawn since T, more than half of what stood at T stands at each of those steps; a stock of seven meets draws of one, two and four, four standing at the third step and none after. A witness of no warning in the level, by a growing draw.
Up to T the carried amount reads only couplings acting before T; a loop forming at T and one forming at any later step carry the same amounts up to T (`Closing.Onset.unforeseen`, a witness).

account_adds.en: The split stated as one thesis with a forbidden observation fixed in advance. 08 records that prose once said nothing sensed shows how near a break is, and corrects it: the theorem assumes the stock is not sensed.

source_adds.en: Hastings and Wysham's shifts with no warning under strong noise or chaos: the account's no-warning laws are other mechanisms, and the record lists shifts with no bifurcation as not shown. Whether T6 says anything beyond the case without feedback is S-16's open question.

name.en: Self-organized criticality

source.work: Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld, Phys. Rev. Lett. 59 (1987); Dhar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64 (1990)

sense.en: A slowly driven threshold system with fast relaxation tunes itself, with no external parameter, to a critical state where responses come as avalanches of all sizes, in power-law distribution. The sandpile's abelian property says the order of topplings does not change the result. How widely real systems are so is disputed.

reading.en: Whole numbers are no obstacle: the sandpile is in whole grains. By mechanism the neighbours fall short: `how-loops-form`'s threshold witness has steady drive and a threshold, then doubling, with no relaxation or self-tuning; traces commute unjoined exchanges, which is not firing confluence; a cascade along total dependence has no drive. I found nothing stating slow drive with fast relaxation, a self-tuned margin or a size law. The regime's draw is standing, so its margin does not tune itself. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: All of it: the self-tuning, the avalanche distribution, the abelian group. 08's table names only chip-firing's order independence and thresholds in chips as stated elsewhere. My remark: a stock self-tuned near its need would bear on T1 and T6; this is unexplored.

source.work: Carlson and Doyle, Phys. Rev. E 60 (1999); Phys. Rev. Lett. 84 (2000)

sense.en: Against self-organized criticality, power laws can come from design or selection optimizing under constraints: a system tuned against the perturbations it was designed for grows robust to them and fragile to rare or unanticipated ones.

reading.en: Proposed here, not in the account, and only for HOT's 'unanticipated' half: what an optimizing order does not read takes the shared constraint's cost. With room, every optimum stands at the least level beyond. Fragility to rare events differs: HOT's design reads their probability and weighs them low, which this law does not state. HOT's tail law has no counterpart. Standing: my reading only. [AI reading]

(a) One step: with room every optimum of an order rising with a family stands at the least level beyond, and, on a web with each condition beyond depended on at a need met at the step, breaks exactly the dependences beyond that some eligible outcome breaks.

account_adds.en: Exact conditions for the drain, room and the outcome set, on one step, for every order rising with the family; 08 says the law restates Zhuang and Hadfield-Menell's Theorem 1. No evaluation enters: the record says the beyond's fall is not shown a harm.

source_adds.en: The trade-off curve and tail distributions from a design problem. No statement here says how losses are distributed by size, and no optimum here is measured on an event distribution.

source.work: Broadbent and Hammersley (1957); Erdős and Rényi (1960); Callaway and others, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85 (2000)

sense.en: On a large random or lattice web a connected cluster spanning the system appears sharply at a threshold in the share of links or nodes kept. Removing nodes past it fragments the web, the threshold depending on the degree distribution. Sharpness belongs to the limit of large size.

reading.en: The neighbours are per graph and exact, not statistical over an ensemble: a set relying on at most its tolerance outside it keeps giving; a cascade down chains of total dependence; points of no return not rising under mutual support. name.en: Threshold contagion on a given graph

source.work: Granovetter, Am. J. Sociol. 83 (1978); Chalupa, Leath and Reich, J. Phys. C 12 (1979); Morris, Rev. Econ. Stud. 67 (2000); Watts, PNAS 99 (2002)

sense.en: A node adopts once enough of its neighbours have. Thresholds rising or falling move the outcome monotonically. On a given graph contagion from a seed stops at a sufficiently cohesive set (Morris, in fractions); on random graphs a global cascade appears within a window of connectivity and thresholds (Watts).

reading.en: The tolerating law is a threshold model on a given graph of waits, written by tolerance rather than need; one record says monotone threshold dynamics, and another sets a critical mass beside Schelling and Granovetter. A thin withholding passing out in one step has the form of a seed too thin to spread. Only `kept_set` as Morris's cohesive set is proposed here. thresholds-of-waiting itself credits none of this and reads onto social viability. No law says whether a seed spreads globally. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type; the web reading on the World): under the tolerating law a formation gives where all but its tolerance of what it waits on gave. A set giving at the start, each member waiting on at most its tolerance outside it, keeps giving whatever the rest does, and a thin withholding passes out in one step. In a triad one withholding spreads to all with tolerance zero and passes out with tolerance one, while total withholding is kept.

Theorem (any type): for the same waits and start, a formation giving under a tolerating law gives under every tolerating law with tolerances no smaller. It shows only that more tolerance gives no less, not that it is better. Correspondence field: monotone threshold dynamics.

With lo ≤ hi a share decides exactly where lo < c < hi (`DrawnShaping.critical_mass_iff`). Correspondence field: the threshold is the critical mass of binary choice with externalities (Schelling 1973, 1978; Granovetter 1978, whose thresholds are distributed where here there is one).

account_adds.en: From total withholding, restoring needs a formation sparing all it waits on, and without one total withholding stays; on a gift web support is a run of the law, with tolerance the number upstream less the need.

source_adds.en: The global cascade window, distributed thresholds, degree distributions, fractions of neighbours and any ensemble. The record excludes amounts of giving, thresholds with memory and how tolerances form.

name.en: Cascades along dependence and interdependent networks

source.work: Pimm (1980); Dunne, Williams and Martinez (2002); Buldyrev and others, Nature 464 (2010)

sense.en: Failure passes along dependence. In food webs the reach of secondary extinctions is set by the web's structure. In two interdependent networks a cascade of mutual dependence can fragment both abruptly, leaving them more fragile than either alone.

reading.en: The chain law has the deterministic form: along total dependence with positive draws the end of one ends everything downstream, a ring together or not at all, and a draw of nothing stops it; a reserve defers it link by link. Buldyrev's abruptness is a statistic of random graphs, absent here. The records credit the food-web work, not Buldyrev; that resemblance is my reading. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (the regime; any number of conditions, any index type): under mutual support raising a level never ends one that held; along every chain of total dependence with positive draws the end of one ends everything downstream, a ring ending together or not at all, and a draw of nothing stops the cascade.

Theorem (World): where the reserve decays, along a chain of embodied links, each requiring the one before at a positive need from T on with the first ended from T, coextinction runs down the chain link by link; without decay each link ends given excluded middle, with no bound.

account_adds.en: Each link's steps counted, positive draws shown needed by a witness, and a calibration: naming when a deferred end comes is an omniscience principle.

source_adds.en: Abrupt collapse under random failure and its threshold; reach as a statistic of web structure, the record calling field reach untested; partial dependence and a cascade's time, which 02's Open lists.

name.en: Open systems: order kept by what flows through

source.work: Schrödinger, What Is Life? (1944); Nicolis and Prigogine, Self-Organization in Nonequilibrium Systems (1977)
source.locator: the entropy balance dS = d_e S + d_i S; locator unverified

sense.en: A system stays away from equilibrium only by exchange with its surroundings: its internal entropy production is non-negative, and the balance is kept by entropy exported, or free energy taken in, at rates the theory quantifies.

reading.en: The necessity is the account's, in amounts: an enclosed finite family taken from without end cannot go unfed from beyond, and over a stretch a stock rises by at most its inflow, which 08 records as the entropy balance in counts. Reading sunlight or imports as inflow is a correspondence. It is one direction, and openness does not suffice for arising without end. The audit says the exclusion is the sources' own and the theory forbids no more and needs more to forbid it. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World; balance and dissipation, equality of conditions decided): a finite family without repetition, enclosed around from some step on and taken from or rising at arbitrarily late steps, cannot from any step on be fed from nothing beyond it. No step of feeding is named. It needs a fixed unit of natural-number amounts.

Theorem (World: balance; local: the risen family listed without repetition): a family's inflow across a step is what each formation taking part gives it beyond what it takes from it, summed; it is zero exactly where the family gains nothing, and over a stretch a stock rises by at most the stretch's inflow.
The eight premises decide neither enclosure nor openness, and openness with them does not give arising without end.
Fed from beyond, entropy, nets: restated; closest prior Schrödinger (1944), Prigogine (1977), ranking functions, P-invariants.

account_adds.en: The premises needed, each with a witness (censuses, embodiment), and calibration at the unit: at a unit that splits at arbitrarily late steps the conclusion can fail.

source_adds.en: Rates and real amounts: a balance per step in counts is stated, yet S-06 says the law gives no amount, rate or time of feeding, which an entropy-production balance would give. How much feeding a stock needs is not stated, and no theorem states the law over real amounts.

name.en: Dissipative structures and least entropy production

source.work: Glansdorff and Prigogine, Thermodynamic Theory of Structure, Stability and Fluctuations (1971); Nicolis and Prigogine (1977); Bénard cells, Belousov–Zhabotinsky as examples

sense.en: Near equilibrium, in the linear regime, a steady state minimizes entropy production. Far from equilibrium that steady state can lose stability at a bifurcation, and new ordered patterns form and are kept by dissipation itself: order through fluctuation. The near-equilibrium principle's reach has been contested (uncertain in detail).

reading.en: The account states that continuing needs feeding, not that a throughput forms structure; I found no law where a homogeneous steady state loses stability. Neighbours take the pattern as given: a pattern lasting through passing does not show carrying forming by passing. 08 itself lists both as stated by prior frameworks and not yet here. Were they taken up, the account would still refuse one reading: neither its generation nor 生生 is any new organization, so a Bénard cell's order would say nothing of direction. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: All of it: the extremum principle, the bifurcation, pattern forming, and the temperature and force gradients that a level in whole units of exergy against one reference environment does not represent. Stated limit: 08's last column of the Fed from beyond row.

name.en: Landauer's principle and Bennett's history

source.work: Landauer, IBM J. Res. Dev. 5 (1961); Bennett, IBM J. Res. Dev. 17 (1973); Sagawa (2014)

sense.en: A logically irreversible step compresses the phase space of the bearer of information, so under Liouville's theorem the rest expands, and erasing a bit at temperature T exports at least kT ln 2 of heat in expectation. Keeping a history makes computation logically reversible; Bennett's uncomputation returns the history to blank.

reading.en: The count is carried for determined maps on listed configurations. The account reads that one merge across computation, heat, extinction and forgetting, as correspondence. It also corrects its own earlier use: the heat bound is no floor of destroyed exergy, so it does not supply the World's least loss. Physics enters only through a stated count-to-heat premise. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type; a law that merges nothing): where a part reads one value p after every step and some configuration's part is not p, no list holds every configuration. 'This is Landauer's (1961) count with Bennett's (1973) history'; no energy, temperature or probability is read, so kT ln 2 is not derived.

Landauer's bound is no such floor by itself: it bounds the heat an erasure exports, heat exported is not exergy destroyed, and a logically irreversible step can be carried out thermodynamically reversibly (Bennett 2003; Sagawa 2014).

account_adds.en: The law at any type: a reset part under a law that merges nothing means no list holds the configurations; narrowing the part spreads the rest. The record reads the finite-rest floor as the counting shadow of Reeb and Wolf's finite-bath correction.

source_adds.en: The bound in energy, kT ln 2, measured (Bérut and others, Nature 483, 2012), its general derivation disputed (the record notes Norton); the physics of the bath and of measure on phase space, since a list has no measure. Bennett's uncomputation (only the kept history is stated). 08's table lists both as not yet stated.

name.en: The attractor of dynamical systems

source.work: Milnor, Commun. Math. Phys. 99 (1985); Conley, Isolated Invariant Sets and the Morse Index (1978)

sense.en: An attractor is an invariant set, minimal in some sense, attracting a neighbourhood or a set of positive measure; the definition needs a topology or a measure. Conley's theorem splits a flow on a compact space into a chain-recurrent part and a gradient-like part.

reading.en: The account uses a different object and says so: absorbing region, drawn into it, with no neighbourhood, measure, or minimality. So the main law is near-definitional, 'drawn exactly where it does not return'; its record is explicit that this is no attractor in the classical sense. It also counts what no attractor gives: counting on draws 0 and merges nothing, so a run escaping to infinity is drawn. A topology-free shadow of Conley's split seems near; that is my reading. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (any type): a configuration is drawn into some absorbing region exactly where it does not return. 'The main law is near-definitional, not a classical attractor'. An open world separates merging from drawing: counting on draws 0 and merges nothing. Record: how deep or wide a basin is lies outside the theorems.
Theorem (any type): courses meeting is an equivalence whose classes are basins; within m listed configurations each basin holds one cycle.

account_adds.en: No finiteness or decidability is needed for the main law; an open world can draw without merging, while within a list the two go together. The periphery's market model does use neighbourhood attraction at one parameter: at β = 1/2 the maintenance end and the depletion end each attract a neighbourhood.

source_adds.en: Stability under nearby starts, basin size and shape, strange attractors, and fractal basin boundaries. The word 'attractor' on the spine therefore does not promise these, and a physicist reading the account's 'attractor' as Milnor's would be misled unless told.

name.en: Bistability, basin boundaries and transients

source.work: Hirsch and Smith, Monotone Dynamical Systems (2005); Hastings, Trends Ecol. Evol. 19 (2004); Dean, Am. Nat. 121 (1983)

sense.en: Two stable states are separated by a boundary, in the plane a curve, unordered for order-preserving maps. Which state a run reaches depends on its start; basins have sizes, and transients can cross what a lower-dimensional view takes for a threshold. In obligate mutualism a curve separates persistence from extinction.

reading.en: The account states the boundary exactly where the order holds: a least level for each recent giving, a falling curve; a partner's threshold not rising as the partner rises. The stag hunt's critical mass is the same shape in shares, where without noise the start decides, and the market has two attracting ends at one parameter. Basin sizes it does not state. A shared shape, read across models; the account does not join them. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem: for giving rising in what is left and the recent giving and keeping a band up to hi, the runs resting below the draw are, for each recent giving, those from levels below a least level, decided at step 3 hi + 3, not rising as the recent giving rises. Without rising giving no level separates the fates (`Notch`, a witness).

The point decides the fate where the recent giving lies on the level's side; otherwise what was given can carry a condition across it (`Crossing.crosses`, a witness). Its correspondence field: with a second state variable a threshold is a curve that transients cross (Hastings 2004).
Under mutual support within a band a run rests and a point of no return does not rise as the partner rises; support can save, and inhibition breaks the order of fates.

Theorem (counts): the rule favours the shapers at every share exactly where c ≤ lo and c ≤ hi, the others strictly at every share exactly where lo < c and hi ≤ c; with lo ≤ hi a share decides exactly where lo < c < hi (`DrawnShaping.critical_mass_iff`). Courses lock one way, with no noise; hi, lo, a, p and c are constants. Record: the stag hunt, the critical mass its mixed equilibrium at share (c − lo)/(hi − lo).

Theorem (periphery): at β = 1/2 the maintenance end and the depletion end each attract a neighbourhood, and the interior point has arbitrarily small perturbations that leave. Record: no full basin, and no stability classification for every β. Correspondence, read by the AI: 'the bistable shape of coordination dynamics'.

account_adds.en: Exact premises with witnesses, the boundary found by a finite search with no omniscience, and an inhibition witness where the threshold rises with the partner, so that down-closure is seen to rest on mutual support.

source_adds.en: Basin size and shape, separatrices as manifolds, and laws of how long transients last. Over the reals the threshold as a computed level is not stated. In the field the curve's fates failed their frozen test (MQ7: 0.39 from 5 stocks, lower bound 0.00), so its use on data is not established.

name.en: Monotone dynamical systems

source.work: Hirsch (1985); Smith, Monotone Dynamical Systems (1995); Hirsch and Smith (2005)

sense.en: Where each component's rate rises with the others, the order of solutions is kept. Strongly monotone flows converge for generic starts and their limit sets are unordered; planar cooperative flows converge outright. Competitive maps keep the order with one coordinate reversed. Delays can be absorbed into the state.

reading.en: Mutual support is the cooperative premise, and the records credit the comparison principle. Discrete steps part here: beyond a band a pair under mutual support cycles for ever between two unordered states, which the unordered-limit-set result allows and which a planar cooperative flow, in my comparison, does not do. The record sets it beside planar maps' regularity conditions and does not call it a step's artefact. So the band is what rest needs in whole steps. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (the regime; finitely many listed conditions, band, mutual support): a run rests within the count times hi plus one steps, ending decided there, and each point of no return, the others given, is exact and does not rise as any other level rises.

Record counterexample `Relay.cycles`: mutual support without a band gives no rest; a pair each of which ends alone cycles for ever between two unordered states. Correspondence field: planar cooperative maps are eventually monotone only under regularity conditions (Smith 1998).

The order, the shape of a run and its rests hold in linearly ordered amounts. name.en: Viability and invariance kernels

source.work: Aubin, Viability Theory (1991)

sense.en: Under a set-valued dynamic, a set is viable if from each state some evolution stays in it, and invariant if every evolution does. Within a constraint the largest such sets are the viability and invariance kernels. In continuous time a tangency condition characterizes them; in discrete time a fixed-point iteration computes them.

reading.en: The 'never leaving' law has this form, for every process and guard: no course leaves exactly when a certificate inside the guard, kept by every step, contains the start. On the root it is the largest region closed under a relation inside a requirement. A record corrected the name to invariance kernel, the two coinciding for a determined law. Whole steps and any type, so no tangency arises. The market's floors are supplied, and its kernel is not computed. [AI reading]

says.en: Never leaving. For every process and guard, no course from a configuration leaves the guard exactly when some certificate contains it (a set within the guard that every step keeps; the invariance kernel is the largest). Scope: no entry from unsafe states, no compliance by actual markets.
